title: The Balance Sheet
lede: The salary Donald Trump says he does not take, beside what the record shows he and his family received.
description: The presidential salary Donald Trump says he does not take, set beside the income, paper value and settlements documented for him and his family during the term. Every figure is sourced.

strip.label: Salary Accrued This Term
strip.note: 20 Jan 2025 to 16 Nov 2026, at the $400,000 a year set by law.

strip.label: Reported Crypto Income, 2025
strip.note: Four lines on his own disclosure. Three sit on entities 30% held by family members, and the form does not say whether they are entity totals or his share.

strip.label: Other Reported Income, 2025
strip.note: Golf and clubs, foreign licensing, royalties. Gross receipts, not profit.

strip.label: Trump Media Stake, Paper Change
strip.note: 17 Jan 2025 to 13 Nov 2026. Not cash: nothing was sold.

caveats.text: The disclosure reports gross receipts. It states no costs, taxes or profit.
Some lines sit on entities part-held by family members. The form does not say which it reports.
The report covering 2026 is due in May 2027.
Income during the presidency is not shown to be income because of it. Nothing here shows money received for an official act.

facts.text: He has said repeatedly that he does not keep the salary. On 29 Sep 2026: 'I don't take my salary ... I decided not to, including in my first term.'
One recipient, the White House Historical Association, a private nonprofit. On 27 Oct 2025 it credited him with $66,000 of salary since January.
No donation is documented after Oct 2025. A gap in announcements is not proof that none was made.
3 U.S.C. 102 sets the salary at $400,000 a year, paid monthly. At that rate $725,000 to $730,000 had accrued by 16 Nov 2026.
A donated salary can be claimed as a charitable deduction. No tax return for the second term is public.

responses.text: Neither the President nor his family has ever engaged, or will ever engage, in conflicts of interest.
It represents one of the most comprehensive financial disclosure reports ever submitted.
Nothing illegal, there's nothing wrong with it.
